expected_claims.claim_text_normalized: DINO upgrades DETR-style detectors via three pieces: a contrastive denoising training objective, a hybrid query selection used to seed anchors, and a refined two-step look-ahead box update.
DINO achieves around 63 AP on COCO 2017 val with a Swin-L backbone, setting a new state of the art for object detection at the time of publication.
End-to-end DETR-like detectors outperform classical detectors when scaled with proper backbones and pre-training, contrary to earlier results that favored classical pipelines.
Earlier DETR-like detectors converge slowly and underperform on small objects, problems addressed by query denoising and mixed query selection in DINO.

Classical multi-stage detectors do not benefit as much from very large backbones and large-scale pre-training as DETR-style detectors, limiting their ability to scale to the latest state-of-the-art accuracy.
